differences.what: Front: a low whitewashed wall, eave 731-733 px and grade 752, one window left (x 1525-1531, y 736-748) and a door right (1547-1552, 736-751), heads level. Built at the same heights and places: window 0.7 x 1.4 m without shutters and the door, their heads level, whitewashed log; the render's window and door fall within 1-2 px.

Roof and stack: the ridge at about 713 px and one stack a little left of the middle (x 1531-1537, head about 708). Built at 40 degrees with a stack at 0.55 of the ridge from the right-hand end; the render's ridge is at about 713 and its stack about 3 px left of the drawn one.

Far end: the plate stops the ridge over the front's right-hand corner (x 1561) and draws the end's roof plane falling from there to the back eave corner (about 1575, 731), the way a hipped end looks. The gable built here, turned to show its end as the plate does, puts its apex at about 1570 px, 9 px right of the drawn ridge end; its rake reaches the back eave corner within 3 px. log_dwelling builds gable and shed roofs only, and refuses a hip on a log building as an invention, so the gable stands until someone decides whether this one picture is enough for a hipped log house or a different archetype.
Its left end: hidden behind the stable's roof, as in the render with the stable in front.
A paling before its far end hides the end wall below the eave; the paling is not this record and is not built.
Tone: monochrome engraving; the whitewash is read from the white the plate leaves.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown}. A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
